updates.text: Clean-vs-dirty control (seed 0): dropping 2,150 random lines gives 15.0 % CER (worse than all data, 14.7 %); dropping the 2,150 flagged lines gives 13.2 %. The gain is from cleaning, not from less data.
Public audit page republished with the tuned detectors (Muharaf F1 0.91) and the full AMIDDA rescan (samples cut on Colab CPU instead of a 9 GB local download).
Orientation model v2: catches all 11 of CER-HV's rotated Muharaf lines when Muharaf is unseen (old checks 4/11); auto-correction lands within 3° on 98.5–100 % of fixed lines.
Colab GPU queue: CER-HV's ResNet CRNN and three new recipes (modern optimisation, HTR augmentation, Conformer), each trained on dirty data and the best cleaned version (seed 0).
Detector tuning applied and all 9 datasets rescanned: Muharaf F1 vs CER-HV labels 0.89 → 0.91 (false alarms 158 → 80); flags fell on 7 of 9 datasets (e.g. Baybars 1,326 → 502).
Dirty vs clean training, seed 0 (our VGG CRNN): full-test CER D 14.7 / HV 13.8 / TK 13.5 / HVTK 13.2 %; toolkit cleaning beats CER-HV's own labels, and the union is best.
Compared with CER-HV (arXiv 2601.16713, same split): their recognizer is 3.5 points better (9.7 vs 13.2 % full test); 94.5 % of our top-50 Muharaf flags are errors by their labels.

Main effort: reproduce CER-HV's ResNet CRNN (pilot on Colab T4), then rerun the cleaning arms × 3 seeds. Later: three alternative recipes (modern optimisation; HTR-specific augmentation; Conformer + synthetic/self-training).
Synthetic grid v1 on 9 datasets × 20 error cells: text errors are caught mostly where model readings exist; rot180 and crops are the blind spots.
Muharaf: ~721 (663–764) errors expected among the 920 flagged lines CER-HV did not check; ranked cleaning list written.
Review deck for the uncorrected datasets: 101 definite + 96 possible findings (local page).
Dirty-vs-clean training on Muharaf (5 arms × 3 seeds, Colab T4, resumable from HF).

Toolkit: RASAM-1 synthetic run on Colab CPU (0.02 units; scan seeded with real image measurements, no model run). On 101 lines the blind re-check judged correct, with reader-based checks: shift 99 %, truncate 99 %, merged text 80 %, dropped word 20 %, keyboard typo 10 %; untouched lines gaining a flag 0-0.03 %. Same types on Muharaf without readers: 1-12 %. Tiered review done by the user (203 cards, 17 min, median 3-4 s per card), judging whether each flagged line's transcription matches its image. Transcription wrong on: RASAM-2 garbled 7/9, TariMa dotting 4/7, RASAM-2 dotting 3/6, AMIDDA repeated GT 4/9 and oov 3/8, conventions 2/6-2/8, AraMS repeated GT 2/10; near-duplicate transcriptions 0/20 and rotated crops 0/25 (structure, not transcription). Mechanical: duplicate images with differing GT 14/17 and 1-2 px crops 9/9 wrong (raw images byte-identical), blank 7/9 (faint ink sometimes readable). Projected lines whose transcription does not match the image (each line once): RASAM-2 ~124, AMIDDA ~71 (24-1,660), AraMS ~30, KHATT ~24, TariMa ~22, Baybars ~17, Omar al-Saleh ~0; Iskandar pending (3 definite answers).

Toolkit: RASAM-1 re-check closed (batch 2: 28 of 30 sheet+toolkit lines have a problem; clear-error precision after gate 23 %, 3.8x random). Review deck rebuilt in tiers (203 timed cards: mechanical x3, judgement x10). Leakage: exact counts (KHATT 551 of 1,038 test lines have their text in train, by design; AMIDDA 581; Omar al-Saleh 149 incl. 7 image copies); score effect not measurable with our models (0-3 leaked lines where we trained). Synthetic certain errors on CER-HV-verified Muharaf lines: empty/duplicate 100 %, re-saved duplicate 92 %, two-line image 69 %, text errors 1-12 %, upside-down 0 %; controls 0.1 %. RASAM-1 synthetic run (reader-based checks) delayed by the user. Public audit page now Muharaf-only (images as files).

Toolkit: the user re-checked the 121 RASAM-1 lines blind (agreement with Claude 82/121, kappa 0.52). Human-based: flagged sheet lines 22 % clear errors (39 % any), 3.8x a random line; reader gate's 12 sheet-invalid additions all clear errors; 17 of 41 unflagged sheet-invalid lines have correct transcriptions. New I10 rotated_crop check (AMIDDA 349, baybars 257, RASAM-1 119; Muharaf 0: its orientation errors are 90-degree margin text). Usefulness without new models: reader-free flagged lines are 9 % of RASAM-1 test but carry 27 % of trained CRNN error (RASAM-2 11 % -> 30 %); Muharaf flagged lines 90 % errors vs 47 % base. Audit page: 10 samples per finding, self-evident boxes, fourth tab 'Does it help?'. Timed findings review deck (1,044 cards) ready. tadqiq/docs/10 §5.

Toolkit: RASAM-1 validation sheet re-checked on 121 seeded lines (verdicts by Claude, pending human confirmation). ~1/2 of the toolkit's sheet-'false alarms' are real errors; sheet misses ~118 clear errors. New reader text gate: clear-error recall 70 % -> 92 %, precision 26 % -> 28 %; sheet-invalid found 30 -> 42 of 71. Public audit page now has three tabs: Muharaf, RASAM-1, unreviewed datasets (leakage table, heat map, <=3 random samples per finding). tadqiq/docs/10 §4. SUPERSEDED 2026-11-05: the human re-check withdrew the ~1/2 and ~118 claims.

Toolkit: per-check precision/recall on Muharaf vs CER-HV (public page Fig. 7). garbled (27 % right) and letter_position (0 %) moved to experimental: false alarms 13.1 % -> 9.1 %, precision 86 % -> 90 %, found 1,390 -> 1,379. New checks: near_duplicate_image (D01n; only fires on omar-al-saleh: 8 true pairs, 5 blind_test<->train copies with different transcriptions), page_outlier (P04, info), garbled reader gate (CER >= 0.4). No-model experiments not shipped: orientation by neighbour window, signature-crop rules, stacked-text bands. All 16 datasets rescanned. tadqiq/docs/10.

Toolkit false-alarm fixes after a line-by-line look at misses and false alarms on Muharaf: dotless ى and ًأ spellings, within-split repeated GT, digit commas and $ / \ in amounts are conventions (notes), not flags. CER-HV false alarms 18.0 % -> 13.1 %, errors found 91.5 % -> 89.7 %, precision 82 % -> 86 %; dropped flags on RASAM-1/2/TariMa sit at the reader base rate. Misses: signature crops with correct names, stacked dates in one crop, wrong transcriptions, one upside-down page (7 of 11 orientation errors). Orientation probes: ink-baseline score AUC 0.85 on synthetic flips (too weak per line); suite_v1 char-CTC CRNN too weak (AUC 0.66, long lines unscorable). Public page: Muharaf Error Audit.

Toolkit precision sprint. Precision measured per detector (Muharaf CER-HV labels; reader-disagreement proxy on RASAM-1/2, TariMa). garbled now uses a character LM adapted to the dataset (other-fold model + OpenITI): Muharaf garbled flags 1,028 -> 331 at equal precision. lookalike_letters and stray_tatweel demoted to hygiene (CER-HV: 0/9 and 4/32 real errors). Result on Muharaf: false alarms on valid lines 28.1 % -> 18.0 % while error lines found stay 92 % (1,439 -> 1,426). Word-level context LMs tested on synthetic errors: word trigram and CAMeLBERT masked LM both reach <= 9 % recall at 1 % FPR, so not shipped; a per-word character LM (odd_word, experimental) adds 10-14 points to the lexicon checks on spelling errors. Caveat: on KHATT (repeated fixed paragraphs, no page metadata) adapted garbled rises 20 -> 240 lines, a mix of real typos and by-design letter lists. Eight figures and a local review page: tadqiq/results/figures/muharaf/index.html.

Outside error reports collected and compared (CER-HV Muharaf, RASAM issues and sheet, KHATT, AraMS, NAKBA). New detectors: digit-system checks (C06), page-pattern clipped_text (I06), off_script at any length, 2-line multi_line. Muharaf CER-HV errors found 61 % -> 92 % (without the script-mismatch category 65 % -> 77 %) at the same false-alarm rate on correct lines (27.9 % -> 28.1 %). Caveat: script mismatch is mostly correctly transcribed Latin text and Western digits, so it is a scope question. Local review app built in tadqiq-platform/app (import, live run, analytics, sample review, export).

Dataset-error toolkit, first full run: about 60 detectors from taxonomy v0.1 scanned 16 line datasets (196k lines, AraMS-28k-HTR included). Flag rates are 4 % (KHATT, AraMS) to 17 % (AMIDDA). Against CER-HV human labels on Muharaf, recall is 88-100 % for non-text lines, 56-65 % for segmentation errors and 54-59 % for script mismatch; 21-28 % of lines judged valid but hard are also flagged. Lexicon-only dotting and typo suggestions are only about 15-25 % precise, judged against reader readings, so a reader must confirm them. Split leakage: every test page of RASAM-1/2, TariMa, Iskandar and NAKBA also has lines in train, and so do 37 % of AMIDDA test lines.

Tadqiq plan (now in the local, untracked folder tadqiq/docs/): the data-QA checks become a general toolkit, paper and platform for finding errors in Arabic datasets. Taxonomy v0.1 has 71 error types (18 built), plus the toolkit spec, paper plan (experiments E1–E7) and an agent-ready roadmap. Next: the user's decisions on name, licence, venue and scope.

Automatic data-QA toolkit for any line dataset (17 checks: text, image, joint, reader, dataset tiers; docs/research/dataqa.md). Validated on RASAM test (13/17 by-eye defects caught, one new doubled reference) and scanned 9 local datasets; AMIDDA test is the union of the RASAM-1/2/TariMa tests (its train shares none of them), and KHATT test shares 67 % of its GTs with train.

RASAM clean benchmark with page-bootstrap 95% intervals: best system 3.17 / 5.47 / 5.59 on the clean test view (official 3.72 / 7.71 / 5.67); no ranking changes. Released release/rasam-clean (447-line manifest, 250 re-cut crops, drop list, scorer); dataset issue drafted, not sent.
Record defect gallery rebuilt: every sample states its error and which side (image or reference) is wrong, with colour page views.

Maghrebi HTR push: a CRNN pretrained on 40k extra lines is no better alone, but a hypothesis-level ensemble with our E60 CRNN plus an OpenITI char LM reaches 3.72 / 7.92 / 5.91 CER (RASAM-1 / RASAM-2 / TariMa), down from 4.12 / 8.92 / 7.04. 5 % of test lines fail for both models and carry 26 % of errors; 13 of them have wrong references (MS 1977, MS 609, RES_MON_8_5560).

The end-of-line error rise is a pipeline artefact. Gemini 3.6 Flash spends its default 256-token output budget on hidden reasoning and truncates 74 % of lines; four more models pile up at their caps. No line end is cropped in the images.

The public Muharaf copy, our training data, is stored at 60 px line height (≈12 px letter core) vs ≈146 px for KHATT. Across all 10 blocks, image features raise explained line difficulty from 6–51 % (text only) to 15–63 %; within RASAM-1 and NAKBA-blind, fewer ink pixels per character means a harder line.
Supervisor tracker and teaching explainer published as Claude Docs (links in GUIDELINES §4). 3090 checked: reachable but empty of weights; E1 needs only a 142 MB adapter, planned on Colab.

Line difficulty is a property of the line: split-half reliability of consensus difficulty is 0.54–0.81 on handwriting line sets (0.23 on page-scale Hindawi). But nine text features together explain only 6–32 % of it, so most difficulty is visual. The image layer (R6) moves up.

Letter level, across 10 complete blocks: medial forms are hardest (9/10), isolated easiest (8/10). Dot-ambiguous letters fail 10–17 points more often at every position. Hardest shapes are medial dotted letters (ف ح ض ث خ ج ش) and small final non-joiners (ز ذ د); easiest are the tall strokes ا and ل. Errors rise in the last tenth of the line (9/10).

Short lines (≤ 20 characters) carry the whole-line failures. Ensembling would gain only 0.8–3.6 CER points. Half of word substitutions are real words, which limits lexicon post-correction. CER-HV "script mismatch" flags are correct labels for VLMs; consensus difficulty finds the real noise (AUC 0.94, n = 7).

Backlog re-ordered: end-of-line check (R2.8), image layer (R6.0), length-stratified reporting (X5), challenge subsets, label-noise review on CPU; E1 on GPU with letter error on medial and dot-ambiguous letters as its new primary outcome.

E1 preliminary (one seed, in-domain): unfreezing the ViT with a differential vision LR (suite-v1 recipe otherwise identical) cuts Muharaf-test CER·light from 36.3 % to 28.7 % on the same 200 lines (paired bootstrap 95 % CI −9.1 to −6.2 points). The dot share of error did not fall (7.2 → 8.3 %). The gain is general letter identity (rasm-CER 32 → 24 %). The held-out panel bench is the next GPU step.

Cleaned Muharaf is public as CER-HV review logs (github.com/SanaNGU/CER-HV, no licence file): 126 test and 1,424 train lines flagged. Dropping the flagged test lines moves every model by < 1 CER point and changes no rank, so Muharaf label noise is not distorting our comparisons.

Error decomposition over 194 scored model × dataset pairs (91 competent, diac-insensitive CER ≤ 40 %). Dots alone account for a median 8 % of diacritic-insensitive error (0.1–1.3 CER points): real, but small next to wrong, missing and extra letters (~60 % of edits). 60 % of spaces wrongly inserted inside a word fall at a PAW gap, against a 35 % chance rate, so models split words where the script itself breaks the ink.

Diacritic policy mismatch is a model-side tax on printed sets: base Qwen3-VL-4B adds 10.5 marks per 100 letters on PATS (raw CER 18.8 % vs 7.1 % once marks are folded). Its fine-tunes drop that to ~0.1. The headline light CER keeps harakat, so it charges this tax to the model.

R0.3 canonical predictions + R2.1–R2.4 (ladder, rasm-CER/dot tax, diacritic mismatch, aligned taxonomy, PAW-gap spaces): characterize/runs.py, characterize/errors.py, scripts/decompose_errors.py, 11 tests. New Atlas section 9. A smoke run that reused an older model name was caught and excluded.

X1: the leaderboard reads overlaps_source from configs/datasets.yaml. kitab_muharaf is tagged in-train in the results matrix, fine-tune cells there are masked, and the Fine-tuning tab never counts it as held-out. No fine-tuned kitab_muharaf score had been published: the 3090 runners already banned it.
Backlog in docs/research/NEXT_STEPS.md (tracks R, L, E, X, S with done-when criteria). Rules and results so far are kept in GUIDELINES.md, and a root CLAUDE.md points every new session at both.

Prior art check: no common characterisation standard for Arabic OCR data exists. The closest is Al-azzawi et al. 2026 (shapes, confusions, label noise; CRNN only). Diacritic policy, normalisation, register, PAW spacing, leakage and VLM behaviour are uncovered, which is our gap to fill.

Characteristics framework written. Each characteristic must change a decision (data, model, transformations, evaluation) and pass six validation gates. The plan now has P0–P11, with error decomposition (the normalisation ladder) moved up to P2.
86.5% of kitab_muharaf lines appear verbatim in Muharaf train, our fine-tuning data. Fine-tuned scores on kitab_muharaf are leaked; drop it from the fine-tune panel or report it apart.

About a third of Muharaf lines carry sparse diacritics (mostly fatha, fathatan, shadda), while NAKBA, KHATT and RASAM are almost undiacritised. A fine-tune learns Muharaf's habit and gets penalised under the raw profile elsewhere.
Text profiler shipped: 32,112 lines across 19 datasets (18 test sets + Muharaf train).
Wave 0 literature note and characterisation plan written.
